text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Justice Minister Pal Vastagh described as unconstitutional comments made by the Csongrad county chapter of the Agricultural Producer's Advocacy Organisation, adding if such aggressive political views gain ground, it may damage social peace and stability.
- Parliament began a general debate Monday on a draft resolution regarding a national environmental protection programme envisaging to raise the proportion of GDP.

- The Defence Ministry is determined to challenge a decision last week by the Public Procurement Council to impose a HUF 20 million fine on the ministry for inadequate handling of a recent missiles tender, announced Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti after meeting his Swedish counterpart Bjorn von Sydow for talks on the planned modernisation of the Hungarian Air Force.
- Hungarian President Arpad Goncz met Argentinian President Carlos Saul Menem on Monday and opened an Argentine-Hungarian business forum in the afternoon.
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze signed an agreement with his Russian counterpart Anatoly Kulikov in Moscow on Monday on coperation against organised crime.
- Members of the Hungarian and Austrian Parliaments opened two days of talks on bilateral relations in Vienna on Monday.
- The Yemeni government has commissioned the Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. to carry out seismological research on a 3,400 square kilometer oil well drilling site in Yemen.
- Three international exhibitions will open today in Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The defence attorney of Socialist MP Laszlo Boldvai has appealed to the Strasbourg-based European Human Rights Committee, claiming his client was denied knowledge of the grounds for suspicion in criminal proceedings launched against him, his right of defence thus being violated.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Romanian Defence State Secretary Dudu Ionescu urged the establishment of a Romanian-Hungarian rapid deployment force after holding talks with his Hungarian counterpart in Budapest on Monday.
- The air force sub-group of NATO's training group opened its spring session in Budapest Monday with representatives of countries taking part in the alliance's Partnership for Peace Project.
- Slovenia's Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler is due to arrive in Budapest today.
- Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha confirmed Monday that the board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. has accepted a strategy for privatisation of the broadcasting firm Antenna Hungaria.
- Former finance minister Lajos Bokros refused to give a statement regarding his plans to establish a bank, along with Szabolcs Szekeres, former general director of the State Property Agency.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- A total of 2.55 milion people were employed in Hungary last year, of which 837,000 worked for wholly state-owned companies and 287,000 in majority state-owned firms, a study by the Ministry of Finance reveals.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Agricultural Market Regulation Interdepartmental Committee will propose that the Minister of Agriculture license the export of a further 100,000 tons of wheat this year.
